A1.justification: Both complete 30-page PDFs describe the same NS-DPO research. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish that pages 2–30, including Appendices A–C, are identical. Page 1 differs only in its date and arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic experiments and Llama-2 fine-tuning evaluations in Section 5, with additional synthetic sensitivity results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original synthetic and Llama-2 experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: The Dynamic Bradley-Terry formulation, exponentially weighted NS-DPO objective in Equation 10, and gradient procedure are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic environment and datasets derived from GlobalOpinionsQA, UltraFeedback, and Helpful Harmless, with identical stationary, sudden-drift, and gradual-drift scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments: DPO and SW-DPO in the synthetic comparison, DPO and IPO in Figures 4 and 7, and DPO and tDPO in Figure 6.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains identical splits, sample sizes, preference-generation schedules, reward-accuracy metrics, model configurations, and training settings.

E4.justification: Discount-factor and sliding-window sensitivity analyses in Figure 2 and Appendix B.2 are unchanged. The drift-strength, change-point, and stationary-setting tests also remain identical.

E5.justification: Both report synthetic results averaged over 10 random seeds and standard-deviation shading in Figure 2. Run information and uncertainty displays are unchanged throughout.

E6.justification: All plotted results and numerical and qualitative findings in Section 5 and Appendix B are identical. No result entries are added, removed, or corrected.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Assumptions 4.1–4.5, Theorem 4.1, and all derivations and proofs in Appendix C are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about novelty, theoretical guarantees, robustness under preference drift, and matching stationary performance.

C2.justification: Explanations of temporal discounting, sensitivity to gamma, and baseline failures are identical. The offline scope and proposed future extensions in the conclusion are also unchanged.

D1.justification: The same hyperparameters, LoRA description, A100 40GB hardware disclosure, dataset-processing instructions, and code-access information appear in both versions.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, bibliography, and positioning relative to preference optimization and non-stationary bandit research are identical.

P1.justification: The first-page date changes from July 29, 2024 to May 27, 2025, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. The prose, terminology, and section structure are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–9, their axes, legends, captions, and placement are identical. The page layout is unchanged; the first-page differences are confined to date/version text.

improvement.justification: v2 only updates the first-page date and arXiv version/date stamp. The scientific content, experimental evidence, proofs, reproducibility information, and research presentation remain identical, establishing no meaningful overall quality gain or loss.
